noise.value: After a noisy attack, add its Noise to Threat. If an unrevealed adjacent room exists, reveal its encounter.

ammo.value: Ammo is a shared counter. Firearms spend listed ammo; Reload cards restore ammo.

search.value: Each searchable room can be searched once; draw one salvage card.

spider_feeding.value: At Enemy phase, a spider sharing a room with a Spider Corpse may consume one. Small becomes Fed (+1 max/current Health); Large becomes Fed and heals 1 each End phase. A Fed spider consuming a second corpse becomes a Chrysalis. Chrysalis hatches next End phase: Small lineage → Large; Large lineage → Alpha.

retreat.value: From Entrance, spend 1 action to extract. Extracted crew keep salvage. Scenario succeeds only after the Ancient Relay is activated and at least one crew extracts.

exploration_capacity.description: Scenario 01 interim topology: each room may originate Explore at most once, producing a single linear cave path. Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng — GDD Prototype v0.1 Page 1
WRETCHED DEMESNE:
PLATEAU OF LENG
Game Design Document — Prototype v0.1
Cooperative Sci-Fi Cosmic Horror Deck-Building Dungeon Crawler

Prototype Design Document
<PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 2 / 31>
Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng — GDD Prototype v0.1 Page 2
WRETCHED DEMESNE: PLATEAU OF LENG
Game Design Document — Prototype v0.1
Genre: Cooperative Sci-Fi Cosmic Horror Deck-Building Dungeon Crawler
Players: 1–4
Primary Mode: Cooperative
Secondary Mode: Solo
Setting: Sci-Fi Cosmic Horror / Survival Horror
Core Inspirations: Cloudy Mountain, Vampire Survivors, Diablo, Alien, Lovecraftian Horror, Stargate
1. GAME OVERVIEW
1.1 High Concept
Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng is a cooperative deck-building dungeon-crawler in which players
control members of a stranded salvage crew exploring an alien world.
After an emergency landing destroys or disables their freighter, the crew discovers a massive black
pyramid broadcasting a mysterious beam of light into the sky. Their communications are dead, and the
planet appears otherwise lifeless.
The crew initially believes the pyramid may provide a means of contacting the outside world.
Instead, their exploration reveals an ancient world inhabited by hostile creatures, remnants of previous
expeditions, impossible technology, and intelligent beings connected to something far older than
humanity.
Players must:
• Explore the alien world.
• Search caves, ruins, and ancient structures.
• Fight hostile creatures.
• Salvage weapons, equipment, and alien technology.
• Develop their crew and decks.
• Manage ammunition, health, fear, and other resources.
• Discover ancient keys and technologies that unlock new areas.
• Return to the crashed ship to recover, upgrade, and prepare.
• Uncover the mystery of the Black Pyramid.
• Ultimately determine whether escape is possible—and whether escape is even desirable.
<PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 3 / 31>
Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng — GDD Prototype v0.1 Page 3
2. DESIGN PILLARS
The game should consistently reinforce five primary design pillars.
2.1 Explore the Unknown
Players should frequently encounter things they do not fully understand.
The game should reward curiosity while making curiosity dangerous.
2.2 Scarcity Creates Decisions
Resources should be limited.
Players should constantly decide between:
"Can we afford to use this now?"
and:
"Can we afford not to?"
Important resources include:
• Ammunition
• Medical supplies
• Equipment durability
• Actions
• Crew health
• Time/Threat
• Information
2.3 The Planet Reacts to You
The environment should not feel static.
Creatures move, hunt, reproduce, evolve, and respond to player actions.
The spider ecosystem is the first major implementation of this philosophy.
2.4 Violence Has Consequences
Killing an enemy should not always mean the threat is permanently reduced.
<PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 4 / 31>
Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng — GDD Prototype v0.1 Page 4
For example:
Spider killed → Corpse remains → Other spiders feed → Spider evolves
The players may therefore create future threats through their own actions.
2.5 Knowledge Is Progression
The crew should gradually learn what the planet is, what the Pyramid does, and what happened to
previous visitors.
Some discoveries should provide immediate gameplay benefits.
Others should simply make the situation more terrifying.
3. GAME STRUCTURE
The game is divided into two major phases.
3.1 Ship Phase
The players return to the crashed ship.
They can:
• Heal crew.
• Manage injuries.
• Modify decks.
• Equip weapons.
• Research artifacts.
• Repair ship systems.
• Select crew.
• Prepare supplies.
• Choose their next destination.
• Review discovered information.
The ship is the crew's primary base of operations.
4. EXPEDITION PHASE
An expedition is a series of dungeon turns.
<PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 5 / 31>
Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng — GDD Prototype v0.1 Page 5
Players:
1. Enter an unexplored location.
2. Move through the environment.
3. Explore rooms.
4. Encounter enemies and hazards.
5. Search for salvage.
6. Acquire cards and resources.
7. Discover clues and key items.
8. Manage evolving threats.
9. Decide whether to continue or return.
The expedition ends when:
• The players successfully reach their objective and extract.
• The players voluntarily retreat.
• All crew members are incapacitated.
• A scenario-specific defeat condition occurs.
5. CORE TURN STRUCTURE
Each Expedition Turn consists of five phases:
PHASE 1 — READY
PHASE 2 — CREW ACTION
PHASE 3 — ENCOUNTER / ENVIRONMENT
PHASE 4 — ENEMY
PHASE 5 — END OF TURN
The following section defines the initial prototype rules.
6. PHASE 1 — READY
At the beginning of the turn:
6.1 Ready Crew
Exhausted characters and equipment that recover at the beginning of a turn are readied.
<PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 6 / 31>
Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng — GDD Prototype v0.1 Page 6
6.2 Draw Cards
Each player draws up to their current hand size.
Prototype Hand Size: 5 cards
If the player's deck contains fewer cards than required, shuffle the discard pile to create a new deck.
If the player cannot draw enough cards because their deck is exhausted and their discard pile is empty,
they simply draw what is available.
6.3 Resolve Start-of-Turn Effects
Resolve effects such as:
• Bleeding
• Poison
• Burning
• Fear
• Infection
• Environmental hazards
• Scenario effects
• Active enemy effects
7. PHASE 2 — CREW ACTION
This is the primary player-controlled phase.
Players may perform actions in any order.
Prototype Action Economy
Each crew member receives:
3 Actions per turn
An action can be spent to:
• Move
• Attack
• Search
• Interact
• Use certain equipment
<PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 7 / 31>
Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng — GDD Prototype v0.1 Page 7
• Assist another crew member
• Recover
• Perform a scenario-specific action
Some cards may provide additional actions.
8. PLAYER TURN ORDER
The players collectively decide the order in which crew members act.
There is no fixed initiative order during the Crew Action Phase.
This is intentional.
The cooperative gameplay should encourage discussion:
"You move first."
"I'll suppress the spider."
"Medic, get behind us."
"Don't kill that one yet—we need to search the room."
This makes positioning and coordination important.
9. MOVEMENT
Moving from one space to an adjacent space costs:
1 Action
Players may normally move horizontally or vertically between connected spaces.
Certain terrain may modify movement.
Examples:
• Rubble
• Narrow passages
• Vertical terrain
• Water
• Toxic areas
<PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 8 / 31>
Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng — GDD Prototype v0.1 Page 8
• Locked doors
• Collapsed tunnels
Movement restrictions can later be bypassed with equipment.
10. ATTACK
Attacking normally costs:
1 Action
The player plays an appropriate weapon or attack card.
The attack resolves:
1. Choose target.
2. Determine range.
3. Calculate attack value.
4. Apply enemy defenses/resistances.
5. Deal damage.
6. Resolve special effects.
7. Check for death.
Weapons may require ammunition.
11. NOISE
Combat generates Noise.
Noise is a major environmental mechanic.
Different weapons create different amounts of Noise.
Weapon Noise
Knife 0
Pistol 1
Rifle 2
Shotgun 3
Heavy Weapon 4
Grenade 5
Alien Weapon Variable
<PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 9 / 31>
Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng — GDD Prototype v0.1 Page 9
Noise may:
• Attract nearby enemies.
• Increase enemy aggression.
• Trigger special encounters.
• Reveal hidden enemies.
• Advance a scenario Threat track.
The purpose is not to prevent combat.
It creates a choice:
"We can kill this thing—but what else will hear us?"
12. SEARCH
Searching costs:
1 Action
A player may search an eligible location.
Searching can reveal:
• Scrap
• Ammunition
• Medical supplies
• Weapons
• Equipment
• Ancient technology
• Clues
• Key items
• Corpses/remains
• Traps
• Hidden enemies
Some locations can only be searched once.
13. INTERACT
Interacting costs:
<PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 10 / 31>
Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng — GDD Prototype v0.1 Page 10
1 Action
Examples:
• Open a door.
• Activate an ancient device.
• Use a key.
• Operate machinery.
• Examine a corpse.
• Activate a terminal.
• Repair an object.
• Open a Stargate-like structure.
• Investigate a clue.
Some interactions require specific equipment or knowledge.
14. ASSIST
A crew member may assist another crew member.
Cost: 1 Action
Examples:
• Help an injured character move.
• Stabilize a dying crew member.
• Provide cover.
• Transfer equipment.
• Give another character a temporary bonus.
Certain crew roles will specialize in assistance.
The Captain and Medic are expected to have particularly strong support abilities.
15. RECOVER
A crew member may spend:
1 Action
to perform a limited recovery action.
<PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 11 / 31>
Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng — GDD Prototype v0.1 Page 11
Possible effects:
• Remove a minor temporary condition.
• Recover from suppression.
• Regain a small amount of stamina.
• Prepare defensive equipment.
Full healing generally requires the Medic or Ship Phase.
16. CARD PLAY
Cards are the primary means by which characters exceed their normal capabilities.
A card may:
• Modify an action.
• Create an additional action.
• Improve an attack.
• Reduce incoming damage.
• Move characters.
• Manipulate enemies.
• Search.
• Generate resources.
• Interact with alien technology.
• Alter the environment.
Cards are generally played during the appropriate timing window.
17. PHASE 3 — ENCOUNTER / ENVIRONMENT
After all players have completed their desired actions, the environment responds.
The scenario may reveal or resolve an encounter.
Possible encounter types include:
HOSTILE
Enemy appears.
EVENT
A narrative or mechanical event occurs.
<PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 12 / 31>
Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng — GDD Prototype v0.1 Page 12
DISCOVERY
Players find something interesting.
HAZARD
The environment creates danger.
OMEN
Something strange happens that may not have an immediate mechanical consequence.
CLUE
Players obtain information regarding the planet's mystery.
18. EXPLORATION
The dungeon is initially obscured.
Players reveal new areas as they explore.
The dungeon can contain:
• Corridors
• Chambers
• Caves
• Ruins
• Dead ends
• Large open spaces
• Hidden passages
• Locked areas
• Objective rooms
• Enemy nests
The exact dungeon-generation method remains a prototype decision.
Potential systems include:
1. Modular tiles.
2. Room cards.
3. Hex tiles.
4. Square grid.
<PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 13 / 31>
Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng — GDD Prototype v0.1 Page 13
5. Scenario-specific maps.
Prototype recommendation: modular room/terrain tiles.
19. PHASE 4 — ENEMY PHASE
After the players act, enemies activate.
Enemies generally follow three steps:
19.1 Detect
Determine which players/enemies they can perceive.
19.2 Move
Enemies move according to their AI behavior.
19.3 Act
Enemies attack, feed, spawn, retreat, or perform their special abilities.
20. ENEMY BEHAVIOR
Enemies should not all behave identically.
Each creature receives a behavioral profile.
Example:
SMALL SPIDER
Behavior:
• Avoids players.
• Moves toward corpses.
• Attacks when threatened.
• Attempts to flee when injured.
LARGE SPIDER
Behavior:
• Hunts players.
• Pursues injured targets.
• Feeds on corpses.
<PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 14 / 31>
Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng — GDD Prototype v0.1 Page 14
• May retreat after feeding.
ALPHA SPIDER
Behavior:
• Aggressive.
• Pursues anything nearby.
• Attacks players and other creatures.
• Does not retreat.
This behavioral distinction is essential.
The player should be able to learn:
"That thing isn't attacking us."
without assuming:
"That thing isn't dangerous."
21. SPIDER CORPSES
When a Spider is killed, place a:
SPIDER CORPSE
token on its location.
A corpse is an interactable environmental object.
Other spiders may attempt to consume it.
This creates the central Spider Ecosystem mechanic.
22. FEEDING
When a spider consumes a corpse, it becomes:
FED
A Fed spider gains a temporary or permanent benefit depending on its species.
Example:
<PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 15 / 31>
Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng — GDD Prototype v0.1 Page 15
Small Spider
Fed → gains +1 Health
Large Spider
Fed → begins Regeneration
Multiple corpses may increase the effect.
23. PUPATION
If a qualifying spider consumes enough corpses and successfully escapes danger, it may enter:
PUPATION
Replace the spider miniature/token with a:
CHRYSALIS
A Chrysalis is temporarily immobile.
If destroyed:
The creature dies before transformation.
If left undisturbed:
The Chrysalis hatches.
The resulting creature depends on the spider's development stage.
24. SPIDER DEVELOPMENT TREE
Initial prototype:
SMALL SPIDER
|
| consumes corpse
v
FED SMALL SPIDER
|
| escapes
v
CHRYSALIS
<PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 16 / 31>
Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng — GDD Prototype v0.1 Page 16
|
v
LARGE SPIDER
|
| consumes corpses
v
FED LARGE SPIDER
|
| escapes
v
CHRYSALIS
|
v
ALPHA SPIDER
This progression should be visible enough for players to understand but mysterious enough that the exact
biological rules can initially be discovered through gameplay.
25. PHASE 5 — END OF TURN
Resolve end-of-turn effects.
Check:
• Temporary effects.
• Status conditions.
• Enemy corpses.
• Spider feeding.
• Environmental effects.
• Noise.
• Threat.
• Scenario objectives.
Then:
Advance the Turn Counter.
The next turn begins.
26. ENDING THE EXPEDITION
Players may voluntarily choose to retreat when allowed.
<PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 17 / 31>
Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng — GDD Prototype v0.1 Page 17
Retreat is not necessarily failure.
Returning to the ship allows players to:
• Keep discovered salvage.
• Preserve acquired knowledge.
• Heal.
• Upgrade.
• Reorganize decks.
• Prepare for another expedition.
However, retreat may have consequences.
Examples:
• Enemies continue evolving.
• Objectives remain incomplete.
• Threat increases.
• The ship may become less secure.
• Certain enemies may relocate.
• Scenario clocks continue.
This makes:
Push Your Luck
a central mechanic.
27. INCAPACITATION
Crew members do not immediately die when they reach 0 Health.
Instead they become:
INCAPACITATED
An incapacitated crew member:
• Cannot normally perform actions.
• Drops or exposes certain equipment.
• May require assistance.
• Can potentially be stabilized.
<PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 18 / 31>
Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng — GDD Prototype v0.1 Page 18
If all crew members are incapacitated:
The Expedition is defeated.
Permanent death may exist as a scenario or campaign mechanic, but should not be part of the initial
prototype.
28. PLAYER DECK STRUCTURE
Each crew member begins with a basic deck.
The deck represents:
• Training
• Equipment
• Instincts
• Personal abilities
• Supplies
• Tactical knowledge
A starting deck should contain weak but reliable cards.
Example:
SECURITY STARTER DECK
• 2× Sidearm
• 2× Move
• 2× Take Cover
• 2× Reload
• 1× Suppressive Fire
• 1× Security Training
29. DECK-BUILDING
During expeditions players acquire new cards.
Cards may be obtained through:
• Searching.
• Salvage.
• Completing objectives.
<PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 19 / 31>
Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng — GDD Prototype v0.1 Page 19
• Discovering technology.
• Trading at the ship.
• Research.
• Character progression.
At the Ship, players may:
• Add cards.
• Remove weak cards.
• Upgrade cards.
• Equip permanent items.
30. CARD CATEGORIES
The initial card taxonomy is:
ACTION
Basic actions.
WEAPON
Combat cards.
EQUIPMENT

31. RESOURCES
The initial prototype uses four primary resources.
ACTION
Determines what the crew can accomplish during a turn.
AMMUNITION
Required by many conventional weapons.
SCRAP
Used primarily at the ship for repairs, crafting, and upgrades.
HEALTH
Represents physical survivability.
Additional systems such as Stress, Sanity, Power, or Alien Energy remain candidates for later
development.
32. THREAT
The game has a global Threat Level.
Threat represents how much attention the crew has attracted and how active the planet's hostile
ecosystem has become.
Threat may increase through:
• Loud weapons.
• Killing enemies.
• Triggering alarms.
• Spending too much time underground.
<PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 21 / 31>

• Certain encounters.
• Advancing scenario clocks.
• Discovering major artifacts.
Threat may cause:
• Additional enemies.
• Stronger enemies.
• New enemy behaviors.
• Environmental hazards.
• Spider evolution.
• Men of Leng activity.
33. THE CRASHED SHIP
The ship is the persistent headquarters.
It should be represented as a physical board or player mat.
Potential modules:
BRIDGE — Mission selection and planetary map.
ARMORY — Weapons and combat upgrades.
MED BAY — Healing and injury removal.
ENGINEERING — Ship repair and equipment crafting.
LABORATORY — Research alien artifacts.
CREW QUARTERS — Crew management.
CARGO BAY — Resource storage.
COMMUNICATIONS — Attempt off-world contact.
34. SHIP THREAT
The ship is not completely safe.
While the crew is away, the ship may accumulate Infiltration/Threat.
<PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 22 / 31>
Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng — GDD Prototype v0.1 Page 22
At certain thresholds:
1. Minor disturbances.
2. Equipment malfunction.
3. Cargo loss.
4. Unknown presence detected.
5. Crew member threatened.
6. Ship infestation.
7. Critical ship event.
This creates a strategic tension between:
Exploring farther
and:
Protecting your only safe haven.
35. KEY ITEMS AND WORLD PROGRESSION
Progression should be partially driven by special Key Items.
Examples:
ANCIENT POWER CELL
Allows activation of ancient machinery.
PHASE CUTTER
Opens sealed passages.
TRANSLATION DEVICE
Allows interaction with previously incomprehensible technology.
GATE DEVICE
Activates ancient transportation structures.
PYRAMID KEY
Unlocks deeper sections of the Black Pyramid.
Key Items are generally persistent and do not occupy normal deck space.

36. WORLD PROGRESSION
The overworld contains blocked routes.
Players gradually gain the ability to access:
• Deeper caves.
• Ancient ruins.
• Men of Leng territory.
• Alien structures.
• Hazardous regions.
• Gate complexes.
• The Black Pyramid.
The progression structure should resemble:
Explore → Discover → Acquire Tool → Unlock Region → Discover New Threat → Repeat
37. THE BLACK PYRAMID
The Black Pyramid is the ultimate known destination.
It should initially appear to be:
A massive ancient communication structure.
As players investigate it, they discover evidence that its true function is something much stranger.
The Pyramid should serve as:
• Major story location.
• Endgame dungeon.
• Source of ancient technology.
• Source of clues.
• Major enemy stronghold.
• Potential communication device.
• Potential gateway.
Its true purpose should remain a campaign-level mystery.
38. INFORMATION SYSTEM
<PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 24 / 31>
Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng — GDD Prototype v0.1 Page 24
The players maintain a collection of discovered Clues.
Clues may include:
• Ancient symbols.
• Logs.
• Maps.
• Corpse remains.
• Alien recordings.
• Men of Leng writings.
• Biological samples.
• Ship fragments.
• Coordinates.
Several clues may combine into a larger discovery.
Example:
Three separate expeditions left records of the Pyramid.
Later:
Their records all contain the same symbol.
Later:
The symbol matches the technology found aboard your own ship.
The narrative should emerge through play rather than through a large initial lore dump.
39. THE MEN OF LENG
The Men of Leng are intelligent inhabitants/servants associated with the deeper mystery.
They differ fundamentally from the spiders.
Spiders represent:
Instinct / Biology / Hunger
Men of Leng represent:
Intelligence / Cult / Knowledge / Manipulation

• Theft.
• Technology.
• Rituals.
• Manipulation of other creatures.
• Retreat.
• Reinforcement.
Their ultimate relationship with the Pyramid remains unknown.

Enemies should not simply become:

42. INITIAL WIN CONDITION
The prototype scenario ends when the crew:
1. Reaches the designated ancient structure.
2. Obtains the required artifact.
3. Activates the extraction objective.
4. Successfully returns to the ship.
Later campaign scenarios will replace this with more complicated objectives.
43. INITIAL LOSS CONDITIONS
The expedition is lost if:
• All active crew members become incapacitated.
• A scenario-specific objective becomes impossible.
• A critical ship/system condition reaches its failure state.
Campaign-level defeat conditions may later include:
• Ship destroyed.
• Entire crew lost.
• Planetary Threat reaches maximum.
• Specific ancient entity awakened.

44. PROTOTYPE DESIGN PRIORITIES
The first physical prototype should focus on proving four things.
PRIORITY 1 — Is the basic action system fun?
Players should enjoy:
Move → Search → Fight → Loot → Decide.
PRIORITY 2 — Is the deck-building satisfying?
Players should feel their crew becoming noticeably more capable.
PRIORITY 3 — Is the Spider Ecosystem interesting?
The corpse → feeding → pupation system should create meaningful decisions.
PRIORITY 4 — Is retreat difficult to resist?
Players should frequently think:
"We should leave."
followed immediately by:
"But there's probably something incredible just around the corner."
That emotional tension should become one of the defining characteristics of Wretched Demesne.
45. PROTOTYPE TURN — EXAMPLE
Security, Medic, and Engineer enter a cave.
READY
Each player draws to five cards.
CREW ACTION
Security:
• Moves toward a Small Spider.
• Fires pistol.

Medic:

• Finds ammunition.
Engineer:

• Interacts with it.
The device requires a Key Item, so nothing happens.
ENCOUNTER
The Noise attracts another Small Spider from an adjacent unexplored space.
ENEMY PHASE
The new spider moves toward the corpse rather than the crew.
It consumes the corpse.
The spider becomes Fed.
END PHASE
Threat increases.
The players realize:
Killing spiders may actually be creating larger problems.
They now have a decision:
Spend actions killing the Fed Spider, or continue toward the ancient device and risk allowing it to escape
and pupate?
This is the type of decision the game should repeatedly create.
46. DESIGN TARGET
<PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 29 / 31>
Wretched Demesne: Plateau of Leng — GDD Prototype v0.1 Page 29
The ideal player experience is:
Explore → Discover → Fight → Salvage → Grow Stronger → Become Overconfident → Encounter
Something Horrifying → Adapt → Learn → Push Deeper
The crew should begin the game believing:
"We're professionals. We've survived worse."
By the end of the campaign, they should understand:
They were never the most important thing on this planet.
47. OPEN DESIGN QUESTIONS
The following should deliberately remain unresolved during v0.1:
1. Exact deck size.
2. Exact card acquisition economy.
3. Exact health/damage scale.
4. Exact dungeon-generation system.
5. Exact Threat implementation.
6. Whether ammunition is represented by cards or counters.
7. Whether crew members can permanently die.
8. Exact Stress/Sanity system.
9. Exact ship-infiltration rules.
10. Exact Black Pyramid function.
11. Full campaign structure.
12. Multiplayer scaling.
13. Men of Leng faction structure.
14. Final victory conditions.
These should be tested rather than decided purely from theory.
